purpose: ConnectToSupervisely connects 3D Slicer to the Supervisely cloud annotation platform so annotators and reviewers can download Labeling Job volumes, edit 3D segmentations and tags in Slicer, and upload results and review statuses back to the server.
summary: A functional, well-documented Slicer↔Supervisely client (MIT, tier 1) with no telemetry, no obfuscation and no AI-directed text. The main problems are environmental and destructive: opening the module pip-installs the Supervisely SDK and its missing requirements into Slicer's shared Python behind an OK-only dialog (no opt-out) and then restarts Slicer, and the module's clear() calls slicer.mrmlScene.Clear(), wiping the user's whole scene including data the extension did not load. Also GUI-thread network work, plaintext credentials in ~/.supervisely_slicer.env, and an undeclared python-dotenv import. Needs fixes before offering to users.

safety.rationale: No telemetry, no hardcoded endpoints, no eval/exec/pickle, and no instructions aimed at reviewers; network traffic goes only to the user-entered Supervisely server. However clear() calls slicer.mrmlScene.Clear() (utils.py:247) and the login token/password are written in plaintext to ~/supervisely_slicer.env (baseLogic.py:47,157-163).

environment.rationale: install_supervisely() runs slicer.util.pip_install for supervisely==6.74.48 and for its missing requirements when the module widget is set up (utils.py:163,167), i.e. into Slicer's shared Python, and then calls slicer.util.restart() (utils.py:208). The only notice is an info dialog with an OK button and no cancel, and the transitive requirement install is not --no-deps, so Slicer-bundled packages can be changed.

packaging.rationale: ConnectToSupervisely/CMakeLists.txt lists both module scripts and all five moduleLib files plus Resources, and all of them exist; EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA" matches build_dependencies []. But python-dotenv is imported at baseLogic.py:29 and used unconditionally at baseLogic.py:78 while requirements.txt only lists supervisely.

license.rationale: LICENSE is a standard MIT text ("Copyright (c) 2024 Supervisely Ecosystem") permitting redistribution; the extension bundles no model weights or datasets. The Supervisely SDK's own license was not verified.

soundness.rationale: Structure follows ScriptedLoadableModule conventions and errors are surfaced via tryWithErrorDisplay, but downloads/uploads run synchronously on the GUI thread (baseLogic.py:223-267, 399-512), changeVolumeStatus can raise UnboundLocalError (baseLogic.py:374-378), and SuperviselyDialog.__bool__ reads an attribute that is never set for delay/comment dialogs (ui.py:173-177).

utility.rationale: README.md has a full tutorial, screenshots, requirements and release notes, and the module is clearly scoped to Supervisely Labeling Jobs; there are no automated tests and no sample data, and the extension is tier 1.

findings.title: Module setup pip-installs Supervisely and its requirements into Slicer's shared Python with no way to decline
findings.explanation: import_supervisely() is called from setup() of both widgets (labelingJobsAnnotating.py:79, labelingJobsReviewing.py:80), so simply opening the module runs pip_install into Slicer's shared Python. The preceding SuperviselyDialog is type="info" with only an OK button, so the user cannot cancel; the only escape is closing Slicer. This changes the interpreter for every other extension in that Slicer installation.
findings.suggestion: Use a confirm dialog with a real Cancel path and only install after explicit consent; keep the install in a documented, user-initiated step.

findings.title: Missing-requirement install is not --no-deps and can upgrade or downgrade Slicer-bundled packages
findings.explanation: get_missing_requirements() only filters on top-level names that are absent, but pip then resolves each requirement's own dependencies, which can replace numpy, requests or other packages Slicer bundles. The dialog text claims "Packages already installed in 3D Slicer are not changed" (utils.py:200), which is not guaranteed for transitive dependencies. The backup/restore mechanism (utils.py:55-109) mitigates but does not prevent the breakage.
findings.suggestion: Install with --no-deps and verify each requirement against the installed version, or install into an isolated environment; correct the dialog wording.

findings.title: Slicer is restarted automatically after the install, without an explicit save prompt in the extension's flow
findings.evidence: 3D Slicer will be restarted after installation.
findings.explanation: After installing, the code calls slicer.util.restart() (utils.py:208) and also on the failure path (utils.py:217). A user who opens the module with an unsaved scene loses in-memory work; the extension gives no save prompt and no cancel option.
findings.suggestion: Ask the user to save and confirm the restart, or defer the restart until the user chooses it.

findings.title: clear() wipes the entire MRML scene, including data the extension did not load
findings.explanation: clear() is called on team change, job change, logout, job finish and submit (labelingJobsAnnotating.py:176,198,301; labelingJobsReviewing.py:179,201,299). It removes every node in the scene, so any volume, segmentation or unsaved annotation the user loaded independently is destroyed without a dedicated confirmation. The save prompt only appears when self.logic.volume is set and only covers the extension's own annotations.
findings.suggestion: Remove only the nodes the extension created (track their IDs) and confirm before clearing anything else.

findings.title: Login credentials and token are stored in plaintext in the home directory
findings.explanation: With "Remember login" checked, Api.from_credentials(..., env_file=ENV_FILE_PATH) writes the server address and credentials/token to ~/supervisely_slicer.env (baseLogic.py:47) with default file permissions. On a shared workstation another local user can read the token. The behaviour is opt-in and documented in README.md:139, but the file is not permission-restricted.
findings.suggestion: Create the env file with 0600 permissions and mention the plaintext storage in the UI next to the checkbox.

findings.title: Local project data is deleted recursively without a path sanity check
findings.explanation: removeLocalData() recursively deletes self.savePath, which is built as os.path.join(self.workingDir, f"{self.activeJob.project_id}") (baseLogic.py:227) where workingDir comes from the user-editable working-directory button. If a user points the working directory at an existing folder, the extension deletes <workingDir>/<project_id> on logout/finish. The path is extension-derived, so risk is limited, but there is no guard that the directory belongs to the extension.
findings.suggestion: Write a marker file into the download directory and refuse to delete a directory that lacks it.

findings.title: Network downloads and uploads run synchronously on the GUI thread
findings.explanation: downloadData() calls VolumeProject.download() and uploadAnnObjectChangesToServer() performs per-segment uploads and per-object removals directly inside the button handler under waitCursor. For large volume projects the Slicer UI freezes for the whole transfer and the progress bar cannot repaint reliably; the same applies to _filterVolumeJobs(), which issues one project.get_info_by_id() call per project on the GUI thread.
findings.suggestion: Move the transfer into a slicer.util.createProgressDialog-driven worker thread or a CLI, and update the UI from the main thread.

findings.title: changeVolumeStatus can raise UnboundLocalError when the volume name is not in the job entities
findings.explanation: volumeId is only assigned inside the loop when entity["name"] == self.volume.name. If the refreshed job no longer contains that entity (for example after a sync or a server-side change), volumeId is unbound and the accept/reject action fails with an obscure error instead of a clear message.
findings.suggestion: Initialise volumeId to None and raise a descriptive error when no matching entity is found.

findings.title: SuperviselyDialog.__bool__ reads an attribute that is never set for delay/comment dialogs
findings.explanation: self.decision is only assigned in on_ok_clicked/on_cancel_clicked, which are not connected for type "delay" or "comment". Any truth-value test of such a dialog raises AttributeError; the code currently avoids it only by not testing those instances.
findings.suggestion: Set self.decision = False in __init__ before the type branches.

findings.title: python-dotenv is imported defensively but used unconditionally
findings.explanation: The import is wrapped in try/except ModuleNotFoundError, but BaseLogic.__init__ immediately calls dotenv.get_key(ENV_FILE_PATH, "WORKING_DIR") (baseLogic.py:78). If python-dotenv is not installed and is not a dependency of the installed Supervisely release, the module fails to load with NameError instead of the intended blocked-widget message.
findings.suggestion: Declare python-dotenv in requirements.txt and handle its absence explicitly in import_supervisely().

findings.title: Global logger level and Data Probe visibility are toggled process-wide
findings.explanation: enter() raises the root logger to CRITICAL and hides the Data Probe for the whole Slicer session while the module is open. The logger level is restored immediately, but the Data Probe change is global and only undone in exit(); if the module crashes or is reloaded, other modules keep the modified state.
findings.suggestion: Use a module-scoped logger instead of the root logger and restore the Data Probe in cleanup() as well as exit().

findings.title: Catalog entry pins a moving branch rather than a commit
findings.explanation: The catalog entry uses scm_revision "master", so the code users install is whatever the branch points at, not the commit 5280d7a this review examined. Branch references are allowed, but the reviewed revision is not what the index will build.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to a tagged release or commit for reproducible builds.

findings.title: No automated tests or sample data
findings.evidence: A 3D Slicer extension designed to organize and manage the work of labeling teams on the
findings.explanation: The repository contains no test module and no sample Labeling Job data; every code path requires a live Supervisely account and server, so regressions in the download/upload logic cannot be caught automatically.
findings.suggestion: Add a ScriptedLoadableModuleTest with mocked API responses and a small sample volume project.

not_checked: The Supervisely SDK source and its license terms (only the extension's own MIT LICENSE was read).
Whether python-dotenv is a transitive dependency of supervisely 6.74.48.
The contents of .github/workflows/build_installation_files.yml, FOR_DEVELOPERS.md, setup.cfg, .vscode/*, the .ui files and the binary images.
Whether Slicer's slicer.util.restart() prompts the user to save the scene before restarting.
Actual build/CI results for this revision and whether the extension loads on the supported Slicer versions.
The exact commit 5280d7a versus the master branch the catalog entry points at.
questions_for_author: Is python-dotenv guaranteed to be installed by the Supervisely SDK, or should it be added to requirements.txt?
Would you accept replacing the OK-only install dialog with a confirm/cancel dialog and installing requirements with --no-deps?
Can clear() be changed to remove only the nodes the extension created instead of calling slicer.mrmlScene.Clear()?
